living_room.context: As the room every household member and every guest passes through, unresolved layout issues here compound daily — this is the highest-traffic diagnostic zone.

kitchen.context: Kitchen stress is uniquely physical: friction here shows up as repeated small collisions and wasted steps during the exact hours you're already most depleted.

bedroom.context: This is the one room where unresolved spatial stress directly degrades sleep — the cost of getting it wrong compounds nightly rather than showing up as a one-off irritation.

balcony.context: As the only fully outdoor-facing zone, exposure and weather constraints dominate here more than in any interior room — privacy and threshold friction matter disproportionately.

studio.context: With every function sharing one footprint, studio stress is almost always about boundary collapse between sleep, work, and rest rather than any single function failing on its own.

open_plan.context: Without walls to define zones, this room lives or dies on visual hierarchy — the eye needs an anchor point or the entire space reads as unresolved.

home_office.context: Productivity here is directly gated by sightline control — every unshielded sightline to a door or high-traffic path measurably taxes sustained focus.
